script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Hey, Emma! I’m good. I was just studying some basic English verbs.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Simple ones, but super useful — to need, to speak, to eat, and to drink.

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: Nice! You can say a lot with just those.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Yeah. For example, I need to drink coffee every morning.

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: Haha, same here! I can’t even speak before coffee.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: That’s funny because it fits perfectly — I need coffee before I speak!

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: Totally. And I eat breakfast with my family every day.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: That’s cool. Let’s start with to need. What does it really mean to you?

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: It’s when something is important or necessary. Like, I need to study English.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Or I need water. Easy, but very useful.

script.speaker: Emma
script.text: Yeah, you can use it in many ways — I need help. I need time. I need to sleep.
